score.notes: A confident Mughal/Taj-adjacent temple face: strong bilateral symmetry with flanking minarets framing a tiered central mass and crowning teal dome, giving a clear base→middle→crown and a readable bay rhythm — deliberate and coherent proportion, though the minarets read a touch thin and detached. Color is the strongest note: an ochre-orange dominant, teal-green supporting domes, with purple and gold accents forming a disciplined, harmonious scheme that gives the building identity. Fidelity is clear and characterful — an unmistakable, grand place of worship with a well-marked central iwan entrance. Detail holds it back from higher marks: the arched openings, gold banding and ribbed domes are pleasant, but the wall fields between bays stay flat and the relief depth is shallow — ornament sits on the surface rather than building layered depth, so no dimension feels inevitable or surprising enough for exceptional.
